card.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{M}(V,W)^{\theta}$ be the fixed-point subvariety of the diagram automorphism $\theta$ of the quiver variety $\mathfrak{M}(V,W)$ for the quiver $(I,H,\Omega)$, defined as above. Then there is a $G_{\widetilde{W}}$ -equivariant variety isomorphism

(3.18)

$\Psi:\coprod_{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}\in\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{v})}\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde{V}^{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}},\widetilde{W})\mathrel{\overset{\sim}{\to}}\mathfrak{M}(V,W)^{\theta}.$

Here the domain is the disconnected union of the quiver varieties $\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde{V}^{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}},\widetilde{W})$ for the quiver $(\widetilde{I},\widetilde{H},\widetilde{\Omega})$, and $G_{\widetilde{W}}$ acts on $\mathfrak{M}(V,W)^{\theta}$ via the isomorphism $\rho$ of (3.17).

Note that if $\mathfrak{M}(V,W)^{\theta}$ is empty, Theorem 3.9 implies that every $\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde{V}^{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}},\widetilde{W})$ is empty also. If $\mathfrak{M}(V,W)^{\theta}$ is nonempty, it is certainly possible that some of the varieties $\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde{V}^{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}},\widetilde{W})$ are empty; in view of Proposition 3.3, Theorem 3.9 implies that the nonempty varieties $\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde{V}^{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}},\widetilde{W})$ are respectively isomorphic to the connected components of $\mathfrak{M}(V,W)^{\theta}$.

Without specifying the graded vector spaces, the isomorphism of Theorem 3.9 could be written

(3.19)

$\mathfrak{M}(\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w})^{\theta}\cong\coprod_{\widetilde{\mathbf{v}}\in\mathcal{D}(\mathbf{v})}\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde{\mathbf{v}},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}})$

where $\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}=(w_{i,\zeta})$ denotes the graded dimension of $\widetilde{W}$. It is clear that, as $(\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w})$ varies, $(\widetilde{\mathbf{v}},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}})$ runs over all possible ordered pairs of $\widetilde{I}$ -tuples, so we conclude:
card.label: Theorem 3.9

paper.title: Diagram automorphisms of quiver varieties
paper.abstract: We show that the fixed-point subvariety of a Nakajima quiver variety under a diagram automorphism is a disconnected union of quiver varieties for the `split-quotient quiver' introduced by Reiten and Riedtmann. As a special case, quiver varieties of type D arise as the connected components of fixed-point subvarieties of diagram involutions of quiver varieties of type A. In the case where the quiver varieties of type A correspond to small self-dual representations, we show that the diagram involutions coincide with classical involutions of two-row Slodowy varieties. It follows that certain quiver varieties of type D are isomorphic to Slodowy varieties for orthogonal or symplectic Lie algebras.
